neighbours.label: the word just before an approximate quantity ('beats about 70', 'sleeps for about seven hours'): the verb or preposition that introduces a rough measurement
fire: A healthy cat's heart beats about 150 times a minute at rest.
Most newborns sleep for about sixteen hours a day.
The average river otter weighs about ten kilograms.
The whole village has a population of about 900 people.
An adult human body contains about five litres of blood.
The old lighthouse stands about forty metres above the sea.
A honeybee colony produces about twenty kilograms of honey a year.
The tunnel stretches for about two miles under the hill.
quiet: A healthy cat's heart beats quickly when it is frightened.
Most newborns sleep in their parents' room at first.
The average river otter eats fish and crabs.
The whole village has a church and a small bakery.
An adult human body contains many kinds of cells.
The old lighthouse stands on a rock above the sea.
A honeybee colony produces honey in the summer months.
The tunnel stretches under the hill toward the town.
